_comment: Emissions catalog — v2.
Supersedes the v1 metrics catalog. The emission surface is now
four-part: register, arc, flags, coherence. Per-slice labels and
flag detectors are parameterised here; code contains detection
logic only.
v2 thresholds are PRE-CALIBRATION placeholders, checked against
the 515-trace LLM-output corpus to ensure they don't false-positive-
flood on normal prose but not yet empirically tuned. The planned
calibration corpus (thousands of LLM outputs across two
temperatures via free models) will feed v3 catalog publication.
Each detector's parameters are documented at its registration site
in shaper/metrology/emissions/detectors/{slice_labels,flags}.py.
Renaming a label, moving a threshold, adding a flag to the catalog
are all JSON-only changes. Registering a new detector requires a
code change + a catalog bump.
calibration_state: pre-calibration placeholders; empirical tuning planned on synthetic corpus

_comment: Register labels come from two sources:
1. Distance bands, when the reading projects onto a reference cohort.
Walked in order; first band whose max is not exceeded wins.
2. Projection states, when projection fails. Emitted by the
emissions API as a graceful-degradation fallback. 'structural'
for table-dominated documents that have no prose-cohort match;
'unprojectable' for everything else that fails.
When a projection-state label fires, the register.evidence block
carries 'unprojectable_subtype' naming one of the four taxonomy
values below. The shape of the emission is the same whether the
label came from a band or a projection state — same four-part
DocumentEmission, with register.distance = null on degraded cases.

projection_states.label: structural
projection_states.description: Content IS structure (table-dominated). Prose residue below envelope; no prose-cohort reference matches. Evidence carries unprojectable_subtype='reference_table' and a structural_profile dict.

projection_states.label: unprojectable
projection_states.description: Document doesn't project onto any reference's PC space. Evidence carries unprojectable_subtype naming why (instruction_format / mixed_structural_fp / insufficient_prose) and a structural_profile dict.

unprojectable_subtypes.description: Tables dominate (table_ratio > 0.50) and prose residue < envelope.

Code/list scaffolding dominates (structure_ratio > 0.40) but prose residue is between 100 and 300 words. Emissions attempts aggressive-scaffolding-strip recovery before emitting; succeeds when stripped residue clears the 150-word envelope. On recovery, evidence carries preprocessed='aggressive_scaffolding_strip'.
Safety-net label: prose_words >= 300 AND structure_ratio < 0.50. These should have projected on the normal path; if they reach here, the router rejected them anyway.
Genuinely too little prose to project on any reference. No recovery available.
